observations.limitations: The definition includes vehicles beyond passenger cars and does not establish everyday preference.
observations.observation: The noun mobil is defined as an engine-driven land vehicle with four or more wheels; oto and otomobil are also listed.

observations.limitations: One report demonstrates natural current usage, not a measured nationwide frequency or conversational preference.
observations.observation: A March 2026 transport report repeatedly uses mobil pribadi for private car travel, alongside distinct categories for motorcycles, buses and trains.
observations.source_title: Menhub: Mobil diproyeksikan dominasi angkutan Lebaran 2026

observations.limitations: Official transport language is evidence of current usage but does not by itself measure everyday speech.
observations.observation: The ministry repeatedly uses mobil pribadi as a travel-mode category, distinct from bus, kereta api and sepeda motor.
observations.source_title: Survei Potensi Pergerakan Masyarakat Angkutan Lebaran 2025

observations.limitations: The entry establishes the sense and equivalence, not how often Malaysians say kereta.
observations.observation: Kamus Dewan labels the vehicle sense of mobil as IB and glosses it as motokar, kereta. Kamus Pelajar defines a four-wheeled engine-driven vehicle and likewise gives kereta.

observations.limitations: Terminology choices support the locale contrast; contemporary contextual sources are needed to assess ordinary usage. The page's separate Malay dictionary entry for car concerns an unrelated sense.
observations.observation: MABBIM pairs Indonesian mobil pribadi with Malaysian kereta persendirian, and pemilikan mobil with pemilikan kereta.

observations.limitations: The article contains inconsistent model identifications; both are passenger cars, so that inconsistency does not affect the lexical observation. One article cannot establish frequency.
observations.observation: A 2024 Malaysian report repeatedly calls a passenger vehicle kereta, identifying it as a Toyota Vios and elsewhere a Toyota Corolla Altis.
observations.source_title: Pemandu Maut, Penumpang Cedera Kereta Terbakar Di NPE

observations.limitations: A category heading confirms current institutional use but does not independently establish conversational frequency.
observations.observation: The ministry has a road-tax heading for Kereta dan Motosikal Persendirian, separate from commercial vehicles and public transport.

observations.limitations: This is an institutional label, not a frequency sample of informal speech.
observations.observation: The ministry describes sales and production of kereta penumpang baru, separately mentioning motorcycles and commercial vehicles.

observations.limitations: This comparative page alone cannot prove everyday preference; the support judgment depends on the contextual sources recorded separately. No frequency comparison was inspected.
observations.observation: MABBIM explicitly maps car-related Indonesian compounds containing mobil to Malaysian compounds containing kereta. Together with separate contemporary Indonesian and Malaysian contextual observations, this supports the shared passenger-car referent and locale-specific usual choices.

observations.limitations: This source supplies only the Indonesian side; it does not compare everyday alternatives or quantify usage.
observations.observation: Current Indonesian ministry usage places mobil pribadi in the private road-car category. In combination with the DBP mapping and Malaysian contextual usage, it supports the Indonesian side of the relation.
observations.source_title: Survei Potensi Pergerakan Masyarakat Angkutan Lebaran 2025

observations.limitations: This source supplies only the Malaysian side. The combined evidence supports usual choices qualitatively, without a corpus-based frequency estimate.
observations.observation: Current Malaysian reporting uses kereta for a named passenger-car model. In combination with the DBP mapping and Indonesian contextual usage, it supports the Malaysian side of the relation.
